summary: Validated the two newly-shipped changes: (1) Guest booking confirmation email + guardrail — POST /api/stays/bookings now sends TWO emails (owner → info@bdsmarvel.com AND guest confirmation), both HTTP 202 via Emergent Resend proxy. With guest=delivered@resend.dev the backend logs both 'Booking notification emailed to info@bdsmarvel.com' and 'Guest booking confirmation emailed to delivered@resend.dev'. With an undeliverable guest email (nobody@example.com) the booking still returns 201 and only an ERROR line 'Stay booking saved but guest confirmation email failed: 502: Failed to send email' is logged — owner email still succeeds. (2) Account menu in site header — logged out shows SIGN IN link (data-testid=header-signin-link) → /stays/trips with no avatar; logged in shows circular avatar (data-testid=account-menu-button) with initials, click opens dropdown (data-testid=account-menu-dropdown) with the user name + email, YOUR TRIPS (data-testid=account-menu-trips) that routes to /stays/trips, and LOG OUT (data-testid=account-menu-logout) that clears session (SIGN IN returns, avatar gone). (3) /stays nav no longer contains data-testid=stays-my-trips. Regression OK: /stays renders Premium/Mid/Budget-friendly tiers; Google 'Continue with Google' button still present on auth panel; booking APIs still 201. Backend pytest: 2/2 new + prior 6/6 trips suite still green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py (~1106 lines) still growing — split into routers (inquiries, stays, admin, auth, email helpers). Carried over from iteration_3/4.

In create_stay_booking the trip_url uses raw Origin header: trip_url = f'{origin}/stays/trips/{booking.id}' when origin.startswith('https://'). Consider allow-listing (or stripping trailing slash) so a malicious Origin can't inject a link to an attacker domain in the guest confirmation email — low risk but worth hardening.
Mixed storage of created_at (ISO string for bookings vs datetime objects elsewhere) — unchanged from last iteration, still a latent sort/consistency risk.

success_rate.frontend: 19/20 (1 false-negative: assertion was case-sensitive on an email the backend lowercases; email IS visible in dropdown as 'test_ui_...@example.com')
